name: Classical Nahuatl
confidence_why: 3 independent first-hand descriptions agree (1 state the same rule, 1 refine it); none contradicts.

new_statements.quote: No hablo en el acento por ser muy vario y no estar ni dexar siempre las dictiones enteras sino compuestas, y porque algunos vocablos parecen tener algunas vezes dos acentos; por lo qual lo dexo a quien Dios fuere seruido darle mas animo para ello, o al uso que lo descubra. [p. 11] ... y lo que en el quinto libro se trata de acentos y otras materias que en esta lengua no se tocan [p. 13]
new_statements.translation: I do not speak of the accent, because it is very variable and because the words do not stay or remain whole but are compounded, and because some words seem at times to have two accents; therefore I leave it to whomever God is pleased to give more spirit for it, or to usage, which will reveal it. [p. 11] ... and what the fifth book [of Nebrija] treats concerning accents, and other matters that are not touched on in this language [p. 13]
new_statements.citation: de Olmos, André (1875 [1547]). Grammaire de la langue Nahuatl ou Mexicaine, composée en 1547, par le Franciscain André de Olmos. Paris: Imprimerie Nationale. xv+277 pp.
new_statements.locator: Prólogo al lector, printed p. 11 (p. 32); also Primera parte, cap. I, printed p. 13 (p. 34)
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened (297 pp, Acrobat text) and rendered pp. 32 and 34 (printed pp. 11 and 13). Both quoted passages are on the page scan exactly as quoted: p. 11 'No hablo en el acento por ser muy vario y no estar ni dexar siempre las dictiones enteras sino compuestas, y porque algunos vocablos parecen tener algunas vezes dos acentos; por lo qual lo dexo a quien Dios fuere seruido darle mas animo para ello, o al uso que lo descubra.' and p. 13 '.. y lo que en el quinto libro se trata de acentos y otras materias que en esta lengua no se tocan'. the compiler translation and reading (no placement rule; author declines the topic; hint of two accents in compounds) are correct for these two passages. However…
new_statements.relation_note: The catalog records fixed penultimate stress (penultimate stress). Olmos gives no placement, so he neither confirms nor contradicts it; his remark that accent is 'very variable' and that compounds may show two accents is a disclaimer rather than a competing analysis, and the later colonial and modern sources held by the project (Carochi 1645; Wright Carr 2016 sec. 3.4 'El acento', pp. 105-106: penultimate, with the vocative -é as the sole exception) supply the penult rule. Describes the Mexico/Tetzcoco variety of the 1540s (the MN manuscript prologue adds that few words are non-Mexican or Tetzcocan, some Tlaxcalan).
new_statements.rule_in_words: No placement rule is given. Olmos explicitly declines to describe Nahuatl accent: he calls it very variable ('muy vario'), attributes the difficulty to compounding (words are rarely whole, usually compounded), and observes that some words appear to carry two accents. The orthography chapter (printed pp. 197-202) treats only letters and pronunciation; Siméon's 1875 French introduction says nothing about stress (its one 'accentuation' remark concerns written accent marks removed from the Spanish text, p. 19).
new_statements.secondary_stress: Olmos notes that 'algunos vocablos parecen tener algunas vezes dos acentos' (some words seem at times to have two accents), which is the earliest hint of a second prominence in (compound) words, but he gives no rule.
new_statements.exceptions: none stated (the whole topic is set aside)
new_statements.identity_note: Olmos 1547 describes the Nahuatl of Mexico-Tenochtitlan and Tetzcoco as spoken in the 1540s (his prologue in manuscript MN notes that few of his words are other than Mexican or Tetzcocan, with some from Tlaxcala); this is the variety the catalog labels Classical Nahuatl. The 2007 thesis (unopened) is a Chilean university seminar on Nahuatl, Quechua and Aymara and may describe a modern variety rather than the classical language.

new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Work 0 (Olmos 1547/1875), missed by the compiler: printed pp. 88-89 (pp. 109-110), Segunda parte, gerunds of the accusative, 'Para yr', entry 'Ti.': the purposive singular is distinguished from the plain optative 'con solo el ayre de dezir, o con poner el acento en la ultima. Ex.: ma nitemachti, ensene yo; ma nitemachti [final-accented], vaya yo a ensenar' (final-syllable accent on the purposive singular; plural always takes -ti). Minor further mentions: printed p. 82 (p. 103), imperative senses 'se diferencian en el ayre del dezir, o en el acento'; printed p. 200 (p. 221), orthography: h written to distinguish words alike in sound that differ only in accent. Transcriptions saved to Work 1:…

audit.deciding_source_kind: database or survey citing another work
audit.reasoning: Coding (fixed-dominant penultimate, non-strict because of the stressed vocative) is correct and is now independently confirmed by Launey 1986:532-533 (vocatives are 'les seuls oxytons de la langue nahuatl'; men's -é accented suffix; women's vocative = shift of accent 'de la pénultième à la dernière syllabe') and by Carochi 1645 Lib.1 cap.3 §1 (vocative e 'con accento agudo, y en tono alto'). But the record's deciding citation is an uncited Wikipedia section, with empty quote/cite/loc/grade fields, for a language with 39 Glottolog descriptive refs including 400-1600 pp grammars. Action: re-cite the record to Launey 1986 §5.1.2.5 pp. 532-533 (now, scanned in scanned/ and) with Carochi 1645 as older-primary support, and upgrade to Launey 2011 / Andrews 2003 when obtainable. no reclassification needed.

sources.quote: Stress generally falls on the penultimate syllable. The one exception is the vocative suffix (used by men) -e, which is added to the end of a word and is always stressed.

sources.quote: p.532: 'les formes vocatives constituent d'un point de vue accentuel les seuls oxytons de la langue nahuatl' ... 'Le vocatif utilisé par un homme est en effet marqué par un suffixe accentué /-é/'; p.533: 'tandis que le vocatif utilisé par une femme est marqué par un simple déplacement de l'accent de la pénultième à la dernière syllabe' ... 'aucun dialecte moderne n'utilise à notre connaissance de vocatif oxyton'.

sources.citation: Carochi, Horacio. 1645. Arte de la lengua mexicana con la declaración de los adverbios della. México: Juan Ruyz. (archive.org item artedelalenguame00caro, scanned text)
sources.quote: Vocative: 'forman los varones el vocativo añadiendo una e pronunciada con accento agudo, y en tono alto' ... 'Las mugeres no usan desta e en el Vocativo pero levantan mucho la postrera syllaba del nombre'. Accents chapter treats vowel length and saltillo; notes final long syllables are pronounced 'en tono baxo como todas las demás syllabas finales largas' (consistent with non-final prominence) but states no general penult rule.
